key_insight: QD-PINN uses physics-informed neural networks to estimate optimal stopping boundaries for Bayesian quickest detection in high-dimensional, spatially dependent diffusions.
engineering_relevance: The framework could support timely change detection in systems modeled by correlated diffusion processes, where traditional numerical methods become difficult to scale.
method: Formulate quickest detection through a free-boundary PDE.
Establish equivalence to an infinite-dimensional stochastic optimization problem to justify neural-network approximation.
Assess stopping-boundary uncertainty using deep ensembles and Monte Carlo dropout.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports close agreement with reference numerical solutions where available and low boundary variability across independent training runs and stochastic forward passes.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify computational scaling or accuracy across dimensions, so practical high-dimensional performance remains to be assessed.
paper_title: QD-PINN:A Physics-Informed Neural Network Approach to Bayesian Quickest Detection in High-Dimensional Diffusions
